acko.summary: Acko is an insurance company with no branches and no agents.
lessons: In insurance, the claim is the product.
Cutting out middlemen lowers price, but you then pay to find customers yourself.
In regulated businesses, a strong product can still be slowed by rules on costs.

scenes.title: Who is it for?
scenes.prompt: Day 1. You are the new PM of Acko. An online-only insurance company that sells car, bike, health and life cover through its app, and tries to make claims fast and painless. Who do you build for first?
right: Young car owner: a 28-year-old in Bengaluru with a 2-year-old Baleno.

wrong.text: The weekend binge-watcher: a 27-year-old in Bengaluru who watches K-dramas, Indian originals and true crime on weekends.
Independent barber: works alone and rents a chair in Manchester.
Corporate recruiter: a talent acquisition manager at an IT services company hiring 200 engineers a quarter.
Long-time Apple household: a US family with iPhones, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch.
Budget first-time smartphone upgrader: a buyer in a tier-2 city looking at CMF phones around ₹15,000 to ₹19,000.

scenes.win: Right. A 28-year-old in Bengaluru with a 2-year-old Baleno. They want: cheapest renewal; easy claims.
scenes.lose: You built for the wrong crowd. They try Acko once and leave. Hint: Acko's real users want things like "cheapest renewal".

scenes.title: What hurts?
scenes.prompt: You sit with a few of these users. Which problem do they keep bringing up?
right: Insurance bought through dealers and agents costs more.

wrong.text: Phones get slow and stop getting updates after a few years.
Smartphones were too expensive for most Indians.
English tests like IELTS are costly and need a test centre.
Branded fashion is expensive.
Fake profiles make online dating unsafe.

scenes.win: Yes. Acko solves it like this: Direct online sales with lower prices.
scenes.lose: You fixed a problem these users rarely have. Hint: one thing that frustrates them is "dealer-pushed insurance is costly".

scenes.title: Build the core
scenes.prompt: You can build one thing first. Which feature becomes the heart of Acko?
right: Instant car and bike insurance: quote and buy in minutes using the vehicle number.

wrong.text: Gemini Live: real-time voice and camera conversation.
Price Prediction: estimates how Advance fares will rise, nudging people to book early.
Spam detection and blocking: flags and blocks numbers that many users reported.
udaanCapital credit: buy now, pay later for retailers, through lending partners.
Nintendo Switch Online: paid online play, classic NES to GameCube games and cloud saves.

scenes.win: Good call. Motor is Acko's main business and entry point.
scenes.lose: Users shrug. That feature belongs to a different kind of product. Hint: Acko's promise is "Cheaper insurance bought in minutes, with fast app-based claims and no agent calling you."

scenes.title: Make money
scenes.prompt: Investors ask: where will most of Acko's money come from?
right: Motor insurance premiums: car and bike cover, the biggest line.

wrong.text: Logistics and marketplace fees: commission and delivery fees from third-party sellers.
Audiobook add-ons: extra audiobook hours sold beyond the 15 hours included.
Commission from cinemas and organisers: a share of ticket value, higher for events than movies.
Compute: selling capacity on Mistral Compute data centres, newer and growing.
K-12 course packages: one-time or multi-year packages, often ₹30,000 to ₹1 lakh plus, many financed by EMI loans.

scenes.win: That's it. Acko is the insurer, so it keeps the premium and pays claims.
scenes.lose: Revenue barely moves, and runway shrinks. Hint, look at how Acko prices things: "Prices shown instantly on the site based on vehicle, age and cover."

scenes.title: Pick the north star
scenes.prompt: The team needs one number to chase every week. Which north star fits Acko?
right: Claims settled within the promised time with a positive customer rating, per month

wrong.text: Weekly members who get real career value: a job application, a recruiter conversation, a new useful connection or meaningful feed engagement
Weekly users who complete a task with Meta AI or Muse (an answer used, an image shared, a purchase or plan made)
Weekly meeting minutes held on Meet by paying Workspace organisations
Paid GPU hours and model calls used by outside (non-Ola) customers each month
Room nights stayed per month by guests who complete their trip

scenes.win: Yes. A claim is the moment insurance proves its worth.
scenes.lose: The team chases the wrong number and the product drifts. Hint: a good north star counts the moment a Acko user gets real value.

scenes.title: Build the KPI tree
scenes.prompt: Your north star is "Claims settled within the promised time with a positive customer rating, per month". Pick all 3 numbers that directly drive it.
right: Claim speed
Claim fairness
Policies in force

wrong.text: Cross-product use
App ecosystem health
Cost per million tokens served
Paid seat retention

scenes.win: Your tree holds. Claim speed: how fast claims are paid. Claim fairness: customers feel treated well. Policies in force: active customers.
scenes.lose: Your tree has the wrong branches, so the team works on numbers that don't move the goal. Hint: "Claim speed" is one real driver.

scenes.title: Grow
scenes.prompt: Time to grow. Pick the 2 ways Acko really gets new users.
right: Google search for car insurance
Cheeky TV and digital ads

wrong.text: Celebrity and influencer marketing
Low introductory InstaHelp prices
Brand fame: 'Tinder' is the word many people use for dating apps
Corporate deals through myBiz

scenes.win: That's how Acko grows. What brings people back: yearly motor and health renewals
scenes.lose: You spend a lot and users don't come. Hint: what keeps Acko users coming back is "yearly motor and health renewals"

scenes.title: Know your rival
scenes.prompt: A rival is going after your users. Who should Acko watch most closely?
right: Digit Insurance

wrong.text: Naukri
Calendly
Peloton
Octopus Energy (Kraken)
eBay

scenes.win: Right. Listed digital-first insurer that sells mainly through agents and partners. How Acko differs: Acko sells mostly direct; Digit uses agents and is profitable at larger scale.
scenes.lose: You watched the wrong company, and the real rival takes your users. Hint, they are described as: "Listed digital-first insurer that sells mainly through agents and partners."

scenes.title: Crisis
scenes.prompt: Trouble. Users feel claims are unfairly cut What do you ship?
right: Clear 'why this was deducted' breakdown for every claim

wrong.text: Show Premium users a monthly 'value report' of ads skipped, songs downloaded and audiobook hours used.
Feed control panel with topic sliders
Verified-fan lottery for mega concerts instead of first-come queues
Clear download limits page with a meter and options to buy more downloads
India cricket-adjacent content and a low-priced ad plan bundled with telecoms.

scenes.win: Shipped. Higher trust and fewer complaints You track it with: claim complaints per 10,000 claims.
scenes.lose: The fix misses the problem and complaints grow. Hint: the right fix would move "claim complaints per 10,000 claims".

agoda.summary: Agoda is a travel app where you book hotels, homes, flights and activities, mostly for trips in Asia.
lessons: Focus can beat size. Agoda wins in Asia by knowing local hotels, payments and languages better than global rivals.
Winning on price brings users, but trust keeps them.
Inside a group, sister brands can cover different regions instead of fighting each other.

scenes.title: Who is it for?
scenes.prompt: Day 1. You are the new PM of Agoda. An Asia-focused travel booking app, owned by Booking Holdings, known for cheap hotel deals across Asia. Who do you build for first?
right: Indian traveller going to Southeast Asia: a 28-year-old from Mumbai planning a Thailand or Bali trip with friends.

wrong.text: Long-term investor: a 40-year-old engineer who buys stocks and funds and holds for years.
Urban professional who orders food often: a 29-year-old in Bengaluru or Hyderabad who orders dinner 3 to 4 times a week.
Student applying to college: an 18-year-old who needs to submit Class 10 and 12 marksheets.
Budget family shopper: buys kids' clothes, home items and basics.
The everyday recipe saver: a busy parent who searches 'easy dinner' or 'high protein breakfast' on Pinterest every week.

scenes.win: Right. A 28-year-old from Mumbai planning a Thailand or Bali trip with friends. They want: lowest hotel price; Pay in rupees with UPI or card.
scenes.lose: You built for the wrong crowd. They try Agoda once and leave. Hint: Agoda's real users want things like "lowest hotel price".

scenes.title: What hurts?
scenes.prompt: You sit with a few of these users. Which problem do they keep bringing up?
right: Hotels across Asia are hard to compare in one place.

wrong.text: AI assistants are expensive for many users in India and other markets.
Writing repetitive code, tests and boilerplate takes a lot of time.
Need a training plan without a coach.
Not knowing which seats are left.
Ideas die in documents because building a prototype takes weeks.

scenes.win: Yes. Agoda solves it like this: Large Asian supply, including small hotels and homes, with reviews and maps.
scenes.lose: You fixed a problem these users rarely have. Hint: one thing that frustrates them is "taxes and fees added at the end".

scenes.title: Build the core
scenes.prompt: You can build one thing first. Which feature becomes the heart of Agoda?
right: Hotel and home search with deals: shows rooms with discount tags, ratings and photos.

wrong.text: Live chatrooms and virtual gifting: hosts run audio or video rooms; fans buy coins with UPI and send gifts.
ASOS Premier: yearly paid plan for unlimited next-day delivery.
Valmo logistics: meesho's own delivery network that breaks each parcel's journey into steps handled by small local partners.
Add-on essentials: curd, paneer, ghee, eggs, bread, fruit, vegetables and more on the same drop.
Rewards and scratch cards: gives cashback, coupons and scratch cards after payments.

scenes.win: Good call. Price is the main reason users pick Agoda.
scenes.lose: Users shrug. That feature belongs to a different kind of product. Hint: Agoda's promise is "The cheapest-looking deals for stays across Asia, in local languages and currencies, including small hotels and homes that global..."

scenes.title: Make money
scenes.prompt: Investors ask: where will most of Agoda's money come from?
right: Hotel and home bookings: commission or markup on prepaid stays.

wrong.text: Late-shipping and quality fines: suppliers can be fined for delays or poor quality, though this is a small slice.
Premium subscriptions: users pay monthly or yearly for an ad-free app and extra features.
RazorpayX and payouts: fees per payout and for current account and payroll features.
Business and Enterprise plans: per-user pricing for teams with style guides, admin and security.
FX fees: fees on foreign spending above free limits and on weekends.

scenes.win: That's it. Agoda mostly uses a merchant model: guests pay Agoda upfront, and Agoda pays the hotel later at a lower price.
scenes.lose: Revenue barely moves, and runway shrinks. Hint, look at how Agoda prices things: "Free for travellers; prices include deals and show taxes at checkout."

scenes.title: Pick the north star
scenes.prompt: The team needs one number to chase every week. Which north star fits Agoda?
right: Room nights stayed per month by guests who complete their trip

wrong.text: Tickets used per month (seats actually filled through BookMyShow)
Images that users save, upscale or download per week.
Number of users who ended the month without an overdraft or missed bill
Weekly matches where the first message gets a reply
Hours viewed per member household per month

scenes.win: Yes. This north star counts real stays where guests got a room they paid for, which reflects value to both guests and hotels.
scenes.lose: The team chases the wrong number and the product drifts. Hint: a good north star counts the moment a Agoda user gets real value.

scenes.title: Build the KPI tree
scenes.prompt: Your north star is "Room nights stayed per month by guests who complete their trip". Pick all 3 numbers that directly drive it.
right: Visitors from search and app
Conversion
Repeat bookings

wrong.text: Output quality
Savings delivered
Build success
Daily active users

scenes.win: Your tree holds. Visitors from search and app: how many travellers come to Agoda. Conversion: share of visitors who book. Repeat bookings: how often guests return.
scenes.lose: Your tree has the wrong branches, so the team works on numbers that don't move the goal. Hint: "Visitors from search and app" is one real driver.

scenes.title: Grow
scenes.prompt: Time to grow. Pick the 2 ways Agoda really gets new users.
right: Google hotel ads and metasearch sites, where Agoda bids for the cheapest price slot
App-only deals and flash sales

wrong.text: Open models on Hugging Face that developers try for free
Buying other companies to add users and revenue
Bank and card partnerships with discounts
Growth in Asia, including India and Indonesia

scenes.win: That's how Agoda grows. What brings people back: AgodaCash rewards
scenes.lose: You spend a lot and users don't come. Hint: what keeps Agoda users coming back is "AgodaCash rewards"

scenes.title: Know your rival
scenes.prompt: A rival is going after your users. Who should Agoda watch most closely?
right: Booking.com

wrong.text: Cash App
Meta AI
Zomato (Eternal)
Robinhood
Grammarly

scenes.win: Right. Same parent; global hotel leader, strongest in Europe. How Agoda differs: Agoda is cheaper and stronger in Asia, mostly prepaid; Booking.com leads in Europe with pay-at-hotel options.
scenes.lose: You watched the wrong company, and the real rival takes your users. Hint, they are described as: "Same parent; global hotel leader, strongest in Europe."

scenes.title: Crisis
scenes.prompt: Trouble. Users feel tricked when price rises at checkout. What do you ship?
right: Show the full price including taxes from the first search result

wrong.text: Publish a one-page, plain-English content ownership promise inside the app, and let business users opt out of their content being used for ads or AI...
'Pick for us' button that plays a tailored title in under 10 seconds.
Battery health tracker and battery replacement programme
Callback support for issues over ₹10,000
Scam warning when a user is about to pay a new contact a large amount after a call

scenes.win: Shipped. More trust, fewer complaints and less regulatory risk. You track it with: checkout drop-off rate and fee complaints.
scenes.lose: The fix misses the problem and complaints grow. Hint: the right fix would move "checkout drop-off rate and fee complaints".

airbnb.summary: Airbnb lets ordinary people rent out their flat, spare room or holiday home to travellers.
lessons: Trust is the real product in a marketplace of strangers: reviews, protection and support make it possible.
Changing fees moves money between hosts and guests.
Growth features like Pay Later can raise bookings and cancellations at the same time, so watch both.

scenes.title: Who is it for?
scenes.prompt: Day 1. You are the new PM of Airbnb. A global app where people book homes, rooms, experiences and services from local hosts instead of hotels. Who do you build for first?
right: Family or friends group: four to eight people who want one house with a kitchen for a week.

wrong.text: Young professional: 25 to 35, salaried, wants an everyday account that helps them budget.
Rate hunter: keeps money where interest is best and moves it often.
Home-based maker: makes jewellery, candles or prints at home; Etsy is a side or main income.
Busy middle manager: a manager with 30 meetings a week and 200 emails a day.
Young bachelor who cooks rarely: a 25-year-old in a PG or flat who wants quick protein without cleaning fish or chicken.

scenes.win: Right. Four to eight people who want one house with a kitchen for a week. They want: space and bedrooms for everyone; clear total price split per person.
scenes.lose: You built for the wrong crowd. They try Airbnb once and leave. Hint: Airbnb's real users want things like "space and bedrooms for everyone".

scenes.title: What hurts?
scenes.prompt: You sit with a few of these users. Which problem do they keep bringing up?
right: Hotels are cramped and expensive for groups and long stays.

wrong.text: No trusted place to learn about markets.
Awkward to ask friends for money.
Paying for many AI apps to get the best models is expensive.
Food is expensive, especially treats and fresh bakery items.
Card payments are expensive for recurring billing.

scenes.win: Yes. Airbnb solves it like this: Whole homes with kitchens and bedrooms, plus weekly and monthly discounts.
scenes.lose: You fixed a problem these users rarely have. Hint: one thing that frustrates them is "cleaning fees and long checkout chore lists".

scenes.title: Build the core
scenes.prompt: You can build one thing first. Which feature becomes the heart of Airbnb?
right: Search with total price and map: shows listings on a map with the full price including fees, and AI search in the US.

wrong.text: Acko Drive: platform to buy new cars online with insurance bundled.
Le Chat: Chat assistant with web search, document upload, image generation, code, 'Deep Research' and memory, on web, iOS and Android.
Vidyapeeth and Pathshala centres: offline and hybrid classrooms in 353 locations.
Chat to build: describe an app or change and the AI writes the code.
10-minute delivery: shows how many minutes delivery will take and delivers from a store about 2 km away.

scenes.win: Good call. Helps guests compare fairly and reduces the shock of fees at checkout.
scenes.lose: Users shrug. That feature belongs to a different kind of product. Hint: Airbnb's promise is "For guests: more space, a kitchen and a local feel, often cheaper than hotels for groups and families."

scenes.title: Make money
scenes.prompt: Investors ask: where will most of Airbnb's money come from?
right: Stay booking fees: about 15.5% host-only fee on most bookings.

wrong.text: Government and enterprise: Grok for Government and business plans, still small.
API: generate videos programmatically for personalised outreach and product videos.
Kitchen appliances: ₹124 crore revenue, ₹43 crore loss.
Individual plans: plus ($8), Pro ($20, legacy) and Premium ($30) a month; new customers moved to an 'X Subscription' bundle after the SpaceX deal.
Muse One subscription: a paid tier for Muse with more capability.

scenes.win: That's it. Airbnb earns a fee on every booking.
scenes.lose: Revenue barely moves, and runway shrinks. Hint, look at how Airbnb prices things: "Free to list and search. Most hosts pay about 15.5% of each booking. A direct booking link pilot cuts this to 6% or 10%. Guests see a total..."

scenes.title: Pick the north star
scenes.prompt: The team needs one number to chase every week. Which north star fits Airbnb?
right: Nights and seats booked (stays plus experiences and services)

wrong.text: Weekly households receiving an online order on time and complete
Monthly repeat buyers across all Honasa brands
Hours viewed per member household per month
Paid members who wear the ring at least 5 nights a week
GMV (total sales merchants make through Shopify)

scenes.win: Yes. This north star counts how many nights and activities guests actually choose to spend through Airbnb, which shows value to both guests and hosts and is what Airbnb itself reports.
scenes.lose: The team chases the wrong number and the product drifts. Hint: a good north star counts the moment a Airbnb user gets real value.

scenes.title: Build the KPI tree
scenes.prompt: Your north star is "Nights and seats booked (stays plus experiences and services)". Pick all 3 numbers that directly drive it.
right: Supply: bookable listings
Demand: guest searches
Search to booking conversion

wrong.text: Task success
Active sellers
Games bought per player
Order trust

scenes.win: Your tree holds. Supply: bookable listings: quality homes, experiences and services available on searched dates. Demand: guest searches: how many people search Airbnb for trips. Search to booking conversion: share of searches that end in a confirmed booking.
scenes.lose: Your tree has the wrong branches, so the team works on numbers that don't move the goal. Hint: "Supply: bookable listings" is one real driver.

scenes.title: Grow
scenes.prompt: Time to grow. Pick the 2 ways Airbnb really gets new users.
right: Direct traffic and app opens, as most guests type 'Airbnb' themselves
Brand ads and free search results

wrong.text: Referral programme paying both sides
Shopify and WooCommerce app listings
Performance ads on Instagram, YouTube and Google with first-order discounts
Accountants and business networks recommending it to sole traders

scenes.win: That's how Airbnb grows. What brings people back: saved wishlists and past trips
scenes.lose: You spend a lot and users don't come. Hint: what keeps Airbnb users coming back is "saved wishlists and past trips"

scenes.title: Know your rival
scenes.prompt: A rival is going after your users. Who should Airbnb watch most closely?
right: Booking.com

wrong.text: Figma
Shopify
Starling Bank
Atomberg
Mamaearth (Honasa)

scenes.win: Right. Biggest online travel agency, with hotels plus a large set of holiday homes. How Airbnb differs: Airbnb has more unique homes and a stronger brand for stays; Booking.com is stronger in hotels and Europe.
scenes.lose: You watched the wrong company, and the real rival takes your users. Hint, they are described as: "Biggest online travel agency, with hotels plus a large set of holiday homes."

scenes.title: Crisis
scenes.prompt: Trouble. Guests complain listings do not match photos. What do you ship?
right: Verified listing check: Airbnb confirms photos and key amenities for top-searched homes

wrong.text: Accuracy reports comparing WHOOP to clinical measures, shown in the app
In hindsight: cut discounts and test real demand at full price
Publish an uptime and support promise (SLA) with credits for downtime
AI music labels and a filter for AI-made tracks.

scenes.win: Shipped. Fewer refunds and higher review scores. You track it with: 'Not as described' claims per 10,000 nights.
scenes.lose: The fix misses the problem and complaints grow. Hint: the right fix would move "'Not as described' claims per 10,000 nights".

airtel-thanks.summary: Airtel is India's second-largest mobile network.
lessons: A telecom can grow by earning more from each user, not only by adding users.
Bundles reduce churn: the more services a customer has, the harder it is to leave.
Free perks win attention but must be clear; confusing terms turn a gift into a trust problem.

scenes.title: Who is it for?
scenes.prompt: Day 1. You are the new PM of Airtel Thanks. Bharti Airtel's all-in-one app where Airtel customers recharge, pay bills, manage home broadband and TV, claim rewards and get loans, payments and streaming. Who do you build for first?
right: Urban postpaid family: a family in Gurugram on an Airtel Black plan with mobile, Wi-Fi and DTH together.

wrong.text: X power user: someone who spends an hour a day on X following news, crypto or politics and wants quick context on viral posts.
Content creator and traveller: a 27-year-old who films travel and daily life for Instagram.
Young London commuter: a healthy 28-year-old who wanted a quick GP appointment without leaving work.
The privacy-minded power user: a tech worker who uses Telegram on phone, laptop and tablet, likes usernames instead of numbers and uses...
The new small streamer: a 17-year-old in India who streams BGMI or Valorant to 5 viewers.

scenes.win: Right. A family in Gurugram on an Airtel Black plan with mobile, Wi-Fi and DTH together. They want: one bill; bundled OTT apps.
scenes.lose: You built for the wrong crowd. They try Airtel Thanks once and leave. Hint: Airtel Thanks's real users want things like "one bill".

scenes.title: What hurts?
scenes.prompt: You sit with a few of these users. Which problem do they keep bringing up?
right: Spam and fraud calls.

wrong.text: Running out of daily essentials like milk and bread
Security and compliance worries with outside tools.
Too many notifications pull people back to the screen.
Trouble falling asleep.
Many young shoppers have no credit card or a thin credit history.

scenes.win: Yes. Airtel Thanks solves it like this: AI-based spam alerts on the network, shown in the phone call screen.
scenes.lose: You fixed a problem these users rarely have. Hint: one thing that frustrates them is "bill confusion with many add-ons".

scenes.title: Build the core
scenes.prompt: You can build one thing first. Which feature becomes the heart of Airtel Thanks?
right: Recharge and bill pay: recharge prepaid and pay postpaid, Wi-Fi and DTH bills.

wrong.text: Smart fans with app control: control via app and voice assistants.
Credit Builder: secured card that reports to credit bureaus.
Bolt Business: Company accounts with monthly invoices and ride rules.
Restaurant discovery and ratings: Search, filters, dish photos and ratings for delivery and dining.
Model choice and routing: lets users pick or auto-routes to Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok and others.

scenes.win: Good call. The core reason people open the app, and a chance to upsell.
scenes.lose: Users shrug. That feature belongs to a different kind of product. Hint: Airtel Thanks's promise is "One app for every Airtel service, with rewards that make paying more for Airtel feel worth it, and quick fixes without calling..."

scenes.title: Make money
scenes.prompt: Investors ask: where will most of Airtel Thanks's money come from?
right: Mobile services: ₹30,943 crore in Q2 FY27, from 37.7 crore customers.

wrong.text: Business delivery: fees from businesses including Reliance's JioMart.
Government grants: smaller funding for the World Service.
Product margin and commissions: Blinkit buys stock and sells it at a higher price (inventory model), or takes a cut from sellers who list on it.
Non-apprenticeship AI training: shorter AI skills programmes and partner-led courses sold to enterprises.
Interchange: a small fee the shop's bank pays when the Cleo card is used.

scenes.win: That's it. Airtel makes most of its money from mobile plans, then home broadband, business services and DTH.
scenes.lose: Revenue barely moves, and runway shrinks. Hint, look at how Airtel Thanks prices things: "Prepaid plans start around ₹199 to ₹249 for basic validity; popular unlimited 5G plans are around ₹349 to ₹399 for 28 days."

wrong.text: Students actively learning each week (should have been).
Weekly meetings with notes that are opened, shared or searched later
Hours spent reading per week across Kindle devices and apps

kindle.summary: Kindle is Amazon's way of selling you books you read on a screen.
lessons: You can sell hardware cheap if you earn money from what people use it for.
Lock-in builds a moat, but pushing it too hard, like removing book downloads, makes your most loyal users angry.
A two-sided product needs both sides healthy: if authors earn less per page, fewer good books arrive, and readers notice.

scenes.title: Who is it for?
scenes.prompt: Day 1. You are the new PM of Kindle. Amazon's e-reader devices, apps and e-book store, built so that buying and reading a book takes one tap. Who do you build for first?
right: Heavy fiction reader: reads 50 or more books a year, often romance, thriller or fantasy series.

byju-s.summary: BYJU'S was an app with animated video lessons for school students, from Class 1 to exam prep.
lessons: Sales can create revenue, but only product value creates retention.
Growth bought with debt and ads hides weak unit economics until the money runs out.
A temporary boom, like COVID school closures, is not a lasting market.

Content creator: a YouTuber or Reels creator who used Sora for quick visual effects and story ideas.
Community manager: runs a free Slack community for a developer group.
Hobby creator: a 24-year-old office worker in Chennai who makes songs for fun, birthdays and inside jokes with friends.
Overseas bank executive: runs a bank in Europe, Asia or North America that wants to modernise or launch a digital bank.

scenes.win: Right. A parent in a tier-2 city who wants their child to do better than they did, and worries about falling behind. They want: better school marks for the child; a head start for JEE or NEET.
scenes.lose: You built for the wrong crowd. They try BYJU'S once and leave. Hint: BYJU'S's real users want things like "better school marks for the child".

wrong.text: Brand advertiser: a marketing head deciding whether to spend on X.

scenes.lose: You built for the wrong crowd. They try Calm once and leave. Hint: Calm's real users want things like "fall asleep faster".

right: Trouble falling asleep.

scenes.win: Yes. Calm solves it like this: Sleep Stories, soundscapes and sleep music designed to help people drift off.
scenes.lose: You fixed a problem these users rarely have. Hint: one thing that frustrates them is "paying for a full year and then rarely using it".

right: Daily cricket fantasy player: a 24-year-old in a tier-2 city who played paid contests for ₹49 most match days.

wrong.text: The retail advertiser: a marketing manager at a home decor or fashion brand who buys shopping ads on Pinterest alongside Meta and Google.
Agile coach or facilitator: runs retros and planning sessions for remote teams.
Working professional living alone: a 27-year-old who wants milk, eggs and bread every few days without going to a shop.
Marketplace seller: brand or factory selling through Shein's marketplace.
Gen Z paycheck-to-paycheck worker: 20 to 28, works retail or gig jobs in the US, often runs low before payday.

scenes.win: Right. A 24-year-old in a tier-2 city who played paid contests for ₹49 most match days. They want: feel more involved in every match; prove cricket knowledge.
scenes.lose: You built for the wrong crowd. They try Dream11 once and leave. Hint: Dream11's real users want things like "feel more involved in every match".

scenes.title: What hurts?
scenes.prompt: You sit with a few of these users. Which problem do they keep bringing up?
right: Paid fantasy games led some users to lose money and get hooked.

wrong.text: Unsure about fit buying online.
Hard to get reports for tax filing.
Starting to invest feels hard.
Running a large online community needs many tools.
Calling clinics to book and then waiting for hours.

scenes.win: Yes. Dream11 solves it like this: Since the ban, there is no money at stake.
scenes.lose: You fixed a problem these users rarely have. Hint: one thing that frustrates them is "paid contests are gone".

scenes.title: Build the core
scenes.prompt: You can build one thing first. Which feature becomes the heart of Dream11?
right: Free fantasy contests: pick 11 real players and earn points from their real match performance, with no entry fee.

wrong.text: Lenses (AR filters): augmented reality effects on faces and the world, including AI Lenses.
Dev Mode and MCP server: gives engineers specs and code, and lets AI coding tools like Cursor and Claude Code read and write designs.
Integrations: two-way sync with Jira, Azure DevOps, Zoom, Teams and Slack.
Docs, Sheets and Slides: browser-based office apps with live co-editing and comments.
Instant Bank Pay: open banking payments that arrive instantly.

scenes.win: Good call. Keeps the habit and skill users already have, without breaking the law.
scenes.lose: Users shrug. That feature belongs to a different kind of product. Hint: Dream11's promise is "Old promise: turn your cricket knowledge into cash."

scenes.title: Make money
scenes.prompt: Investors ask: where will most of Dream11's money come from?
right: Platform fee on paid contests (ended): Dream11 kept a share of each entry pool, often estimated at 10% to 20%.

wrong.text: Collab seats: low-cost seats for PMs, marketers and others who use FigJam and Slides or comment.
Strategic value: data and engagement that help Google's wider business in India, like Android, Ads and Play.
Cost per booking: some partners pay a fee or share when a booking happens.
Business messaging: businesses pay for WhatsApp messages and AI agents that serve customers.
Services: ads: Etsy Ads (sellers pay per click) and Offsite Ads (12% to 15% of sales Etsy brings from outside).

scenes.win: That's it. Dream11 used to make money from one thing: a cut of every paid contest entry.
scenes.lose: Revenue barely moves, and runway shrinks. Hint, look at how Dream11 prices things: "Free to use since October 2025. No paid contests."

scenes.title: Pick the north star
scenes.prompt: The team needs one number to chase every week. Which north star fits Dream11?
right: Weekly match-day engaged fans (users who make a free team or join a live room on a match day)

wrong.text: Number of trips and place visits completed with Maps each week
Number of buyer and tenant enquiries sent to agents each month
Weekly meetings with notes that are opened, shared or searched later
Number of questions answered successfully per day, where the user's need is met without searching again
Appointments completed through Fresha each month

scenes.win: Yes. In the free model, value is how often fans use the app to enjoy a match.
scenes.lose: The team chases the wrong number and the product drifts. Hint: a good north star counts the moment a Dream11 user gets real value.

scenes.title: Build the KPI tree
scenes.prompt: Your north star is "Weekly match-day engaged fans (users who make a free team or join a live room on a match day)". Pick all 3 numbers that directly drive it.
right: Match-day reach
Free team creation rate
Live room participation

wrong.text: Orders per buyer
Weekly active users
Repeat guests
Booking conversion

scenes.win: Your tree holds. Match-day reach: users who open the app on a match day. Free team creation rate: share of visitors who make a fantasy team. Live room participation: share of users who join a community room or stream.
scenes.lose: Your tree has the wrong branches, so the team works on numbers that don't move the goal. Hint: "Match-day reach" is one real driver.

scenes.title: Grow
scenes.prompt: Time to grow. Pick the 2 ways Dream11 really gets new users.
right: Huge existing user base and brand from years of TV ads and team sponsorships
IPL and India match seasons, when cricket interest peaks

wrong.text: Digital ads with a purity message
Activities shared to Instagram and other social apps
Native product sales that bring new households onto the app
Trends and sounds that spill into culture, news and music charts

scenes.win: That's how Dream11 grows. What brings people back: every match is a new reason to make a team
scenes.lose: You spend a lot and users don't come. Hint: what keeps Dream11 users coming back is "every match is a new reason to make a team"

scenes.title: Know your rival
scenes.prompt: A rival is going after your users. Who should Dream11 watch most closely?
right: JioHotstar

wrong.text: Zilch
OpenEvidence
Deliveroo
Nintendo Switch 2
Atomberg

scenes.win: Right. Streams IPL and India cricket, adds free fantasy and prediction games. How Dream11 differs: JioHotstar owns the video. Dream11 must be the companion app, which is a weaker spot.
scenes.lose: You watched the wrong company, and the real rival takes your users. Hint, they are described as: "Streams IPL and India cricket, adds free fantasy and prediction games."

scenes.title: Crisis
scenes.prompt: Trouble. Free contests lack excitement. What do you ship?
right: Season-long free leagues with real-world rewards like match tickets and jerseys, paid by sponsors

wrong.text: Real-time sold status sync with dealer systems
Advance-free streak rewards
Launch in Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru with college and workplace campaigns and filters for religion, language and family plans
Clear status page for each card type's support
Price calculator in the app that shows next year's bill as contacts grow

scenes.win: Shipped. More match-day engagement and a clear product to sell to brands. You track it with: weekly match-day engaged fans.
scenes.lose: The fix misses the problem and complaints grow. Hint: the right fix would move "weekly match-day engaged fans".

dunzo.summary: Dunzo started in 2014 as a WhatsApp number: you messaged what you needed, like keys from home or medicine from a shop, and a rider fetched it.
lessons: Do not abandon what makes you different.
In quick commerce, scale wins. Fixed costs per store mean the player with the most orders per store has the best economics.
Discounts can hide a product problem.

scenes.title: Who is it for?
scenes.prompt: Day 1. You are the new PM of Dunzo. A Bengaluru app that would pick up and drop anything in the city, which became an early 15-minute grocery service and then collapsed by early 2025. Who do you build for first?
right: Busy Bengaluru techie: a young professional who used Dunzo to send keys, get food from a specific shop or buy medicine late at night.

wrong.text: Young Indian user: a 22-year-old in Mumbai who uses Instagram daily and tried Threads.
Budget-conscious suburban parent: 35, two kids, does one big weekly grocery shop and many top-ups.
Small-town first-time buyer: a shop owner in a tier-3 town who has never bought health insurance.
Small-town JEE or NEET aspirant: a 16-year-old in a tier-2 or tier-3 town whose family cannot afford Kota fees or moving away.
Woman tracking cycle and fertility: a 31-year-old planning a pregnancy.

scenes.win: Right. A young professional who used Dunzo to send keys, get food from a specific shop or buy medicine late at night. They want: save time on small errands; get things from a specific shop, not just a big store.
scenes.lose: You built for the wrong crowd. They try Dunzo once and leave. Hint: Dunzo's real users want things like "save time on small errands".

scenes.title: What hurts?
scenes.prompt: You sit with a few of these users. Which problem do they keep bringing up?
right: No time to run small errands like picking up a parcel or keys

wrong.text: Building a store took developers and months.
Screening hundreds of applications takes time.
Design files emailed back and forth, with nobody sure which version is final.
No store in small towns.
Diagrams in many tools get out of date.

scenes.win: Yes. Dunzo solves it like this: Pick up and drop anything within the city.
scenes.lose: You fixed a problem these users rarely have. Hint: one thing that frustrates them is "delivery fees rising over time".

scenes.title: Build the core
scenes.prompt: You can build one thing first. Which feature becomes the heart of Dunzo?
right: Pick Up and Drop: send any item across the city with a rider.

wrong.text: Lossless audio: CD-quality and higher audio for Premium users.
Digital khata (credit ledger): record udhar (credit given) and jama (money received) for each customer with a running balance.
AI Overviews: AI summary at the top of many results pages, with links.
Before-7 am doorstep delivery: silent drop at the door, often in a bag hung on the handle.
Variations and upscale: make new versions of an image you like, or a bigger, sharper version.

scenes.win: Good call. A unique, loved use case that built the brand, but hard to make money on.
scenes.lose: Users shrug. That feature belongs to a different kind of product. Hint: Dunzo's promise is "At its best: one app that could get anything from anywhere in your city to your door within an hour, and later groceries in about..."

scenes.title: Make money
scenes.prompt: Investors ask: where will most of Dunzo's money come from?
right: Delivery fees: charged on pick-up-and-drop and shop orders.

wrong.text: Advertising: ads on videos, Shorts and TV, sold through Google Ads.
Buyer protection fee: about £0.70 plus 5% of the item price on every UK order; the largest share of revenue.
Self-serve plans: starter (about $29 a month) and Creator (about $89 a month) with video minute limits.
Extra generations: users could buy more videos after hitting the free daily limit.
Prime and audiobooks: prime Reading is a Prime perk, and Audible audiobooks sync with Kindle books through Whispersync for Voice.

scenes.win: That's it. Dunzo made money from delivery fees and a cut of orders from partner shops.
scenes.lose: Revenue barely moves, and runway shrinks. Hint, look at how Dunzo prices things: "Not public now; the service has shut down."

scenes.title: Pick the north star
scenes.prompt: The team needs one number to chase every week. Which north star fits Dunzo?
right: Completed deliveries per week that arrived on time (what Dunzo should have tracked)

wrong.text: Students actively learning each week (should have been).
Weekly active merchants who record at least one transaction
Weekly active glasses wearers who use at least one smart feature (capture, audio or AI)
Minutes of Synthesia video watched by viewers each month
Paid driverless rides completed per week

scenes.win: Yes. A north star metric is the one number that shows users get value.
scenes.lose: The team chases the wrong number and the product drifts. Hint: a good north star counts the moment a Dunzo user gets real value.

scenes.title: Build the KPI tree
scenes.prompt: Your north star is "Completed deliveries per week that arrived on time (what Dunzo should have tracked)". Pick all 3 numbers that directly drive it.
right: Orders per dark store per day
Order quality
Delivery speed

wrong.text: Retail conversion
New builders activated
Revenue per user
Own-brand share

scenes.win: Your tree holds. Orders per dark store per day: the key number that decides if a store covers its costs. Order quality: orders delivered complete, fresh and correctly priced. Delivery speed: how often the promised time is met.
scenes.lose: Your tree has the wrong branches, so the team works on numbers that don't move the goal. Hint: "Orders per dark store per day" is one real driver.

scenes.title: Grow
scenes.prompt: Time to grow. Pick the 2 ways Dunzo really gets new users.
right: Word of mouth in Bengaluru for its unusual 'anything' errands
Witty social media and outdoor ads

wrong.text: New products (Make, Sites, Slides, Buzz) bring in non-designers
Sharing supply with Booking.com
Own brands sold on other platforms that bring people back to Nykaa
Brand and premium status

scenes.win: That's how Dunzo grows. What brings people back: unique errand use cases nobody else served
scenes.lose: You spend a lot and users don't come. Hint: what keeps Dunzo users coming back is "unique errand use cases nobody else served"

scenes.title: Know your rival
scenes.prompt: A rival is going after your users. Who should Dunzo watch most closely?
right: Blinkit

wrong.text: Calm
Kuku FM
Apple Vision Pro / iPhone
Zopa
Krutrim

scenes.win: Right. Quick commerce leader with over 1,000 dark stores and Zomato's backing. How Dunzo differs: Dunzo had fewer stores, smaller range and less money.
scenes.lose: You watched the wrong company, and the real rival takes your users. Hint, they are described as: "Quick commerce leader with over 1,000 dark stores and Zomato's backing."

scenes.title: Crisis
scenes.prompt: Trouble. Dunzo gave up its unique business to fight in a crowded one. What do you ship?
right: In hindsight: stay focused on errands and local-shop marketplace, and charge for it

wrong.text: Show a 'Sponsored' label on Prime-boosted results and a separate 'Top rated' sort
Trial versions for every first-party game
Simpler Clubcard for older customers with a printed monthly savings summary.
Neighbourhood referral offer that rewards whole housing societies
Bundle GoCardless into Mollie checkout for European merchants

scenes.win: Shipped. Smaller but more defensible business with lower capital needs. You track it with: contribution margin per errand order.
scenes.lose: The fix misses the problem and complaints grow. Hint: the right fix would move "contribution margin per errand order".

duolingo.summary: Duolingo turns learning a language into a mobile game.
lessons: Habit loops like streaks, leagues and reminders can drive retention better than content alone.
How you talk about AI matters. A memo about replacing people with AI cost Duolingo goodwill, even as AI improved the product.
Sometimes it is right to earn less now to grow users.

scenes.title: Who is it for?
scenes.prompt: Day 1. You are the new PM of Duolingo. A free, game-like app for learning languages, maths, music and chess in short daily lessons. Who do you build for first?
right: Casual learner: a 25-year-old in Mumbai learning Spanish or Japanese for fun, five minutes before bed.

wrong.text: Small hotel owner in Asia: runs a 20-room guesthouse in Ooty or Chiang Mai.
Everyday Gemini user: a college student in Pune using Gemini on an Android phone for study, translation and photo questions.
The everyday recipe saver: a busy parent who searches 'easy dinner' or 'high protein breakfast' on Pinterest every week.
Eco-minded young adult: 18 to 28, prefers second-hand over Shein or Primark for cost and environmental reasons.
Chinese manufacturer: factory owner who wants to sell abroad without building a brand.

scenes.win: Right. A 25-year-old in Mumbai learning Spanish or Japanese for fun, five minutes before bed. They want: keep a streak; learn basics before a trip.
scenes.lose: You built for the wrong crowd. They try Duolingo once and leave. Hint: Duolingo's real users want things like "keep a streak".

scenes.title: What hurts?
scenes.prompt: You sit with a few of these users. Which problem do they keep bringing up?
right: Language classes are expensive and need fixed times.

wrong.text: Paying cash and haggling
Cycle tracking by app logging is unreliable.
Poor sleep without knowing why.
Reading long books is hard for busy or less literate users.
People feel guilty about food waste but do not know how to help.

scenes.win: Yes. Duolingo solves it like this: Free lessons on your phone, any time.
scenes.lose: You fixed a problem these users rarely have. Hint: one thing that frustrates them is "ads and energy limits".

scenes.title: Build the core
scenes.prompt: You can build one thing first. Which feature becomes the heart of Duolingo?
right: Streaks: counts how many days in a row you have practised.

wrong.text: Airtel Finance and Payments Bank: loans, credit cards, gold loans, FDs and payments.
Live bus tracking: shows where the bus is on the map and sends alerts before boarding.
Auto-save: algorithm moves small amounts every few days based on your bank data.
Acquiring licences: settles payments directly in many countries.
RTO protection: flags risky COD orders and confirms with buyers.

scenes.win: Good call. The strongest habit hook; losing a long streak feels painful, so people come back.
scenes.lose: Users shrug. That feature belongs to a different kind of product. Hint: Duolingo's promise is "Learn a language for free, a few minutes a day, in a way that feels like a game instead of homework."

scenes.title: Make money
scenes.prompt: Investors ask: where will most of Duolingo's money come from?
right: Subscriptions (Super, family plans): $270 million in Q3 2026, up 18%.

wrong.text: Partnerships: deals with big chains and brands.
Mental health, menopause, testosterone and other: newer categories; testosterone and Peptides Plus launched in late 2026.
Manufacturer and agency ads: carmakers pay for display ads.
Team and Enterprise seats: per-user fees for businesses, plus usage charges for heavy agent work.
Teams and Enterprise seats: per-user monthly pricing with admin and privacy controls; about $2.6 billion of business revenue run rate in June 2026.

scenes.win: That's it. Duolingo makes money from four things: Super subscriptions (most of it), ads shown to free users, the Duolingo English Test, and in-app purchases like streak repairs.
scenes.lose: Revenue barely moves, and runway shrinks. Hint, look at how Duolingo prices things: "Free with ads and limited energy."

scenes.prompt: The team needs one number to chase every week. Which north star fits Duolingo?
right: Daily active learners (DAUs)

wrong.text: Orders delivered successfully on the first attempt for active sellers per month
AI-written lines of code accepted and kept by developers each week
Weekly users who save or click through on at least one Pin
Miles driven by Wayve AI in customer vehicles per month
Weekly minutes of content watched or listened to in a user's own language, per active user

scenes.win: Yes. Duolingo's mission is to get people learning every day.
scenes.lose: The team chases the wrong number and the product drifts. Hint: a good north star counts the moment a Duolingo user gets real value.

right: New user activation
Current user retention
Resurrected users

Paid seat expansion
Monthly transacting actives
Kept rate after 7 days

scenes.lose: Your tree has the wrong branches, so the team works on numbers that don't move the goal. Hint: "New user activation" is one real driver.

Free app with no barrier to start

wrong.text: Holiday gifting through big retailers
IPL and India match seasons, when cricket interest peaks

Sky Glass and Stream for homes that cannot have a dish

ixigo

Interest balance nudges for returning NRIs
Campus and interest-based events booked through Tinder

scenes.lose: The fix misses the problem and complaints grow. Hint: the right fix would move "speaking exercises per user and trial starts".

ebay.summary: eBay is a giant online flea market.
lessons: When you cannot win the whole market, pick niches where you are strong.
Ads can become a second business, but too many ads hurt search quality and anger sellers.
Trust features like authentication unlock high-value categories.

scenes.title: Who is it for?
scenes.prompt: Day 1. You are the new PM of eBay. An online marketplace where millions of people and small shops sell used, collectible and new items to buyers around the world. Who do you build for first?
right: Trading card collector: 25 to 45, buys and sells Pokemon or sports cards every week, spends thousands a year.

wrong.text: First-time home saver: 23 to 32, renting, saving for a deposit on a first home.
Car owner renewing: owns a 4-year-old Hyundai Creta and renews every year.
Restaurant owner: owns a cloud kitchen and one dine-in outlet; 50% of revenue comes from delivery apps.
The privacy-minded power user: a tech worker who uses Telegram on phone, laptop and tablet, likes usernames instead of numbers and uses...
Serious options trader: a 34-year-old full-time trader in Mumbai trading Nifty options daily.

scenes.win: Right. 25 to 45, buys and sells Pokemon or sports cards every week, spends thousands a year. They want: find a specific rare card at a fair price; know the card is real.
scenes.lose: You built for the wrong crowd. They try eBay once and leave. Hint: eBay's real users want things like "find a specific rare card at a fair price".

scenes.title: What hurts?
scenes.prompt: You sit with a few of these users. Which problem do they keep bringing up?
right: Rare or used items are hard to find in normal shops.

wrong.text: Last-minute gifts for birthdays or festivals
Support teams answer the same questions again and again.
Live cricket used to need a costly TV cable connection.
Small Asian hotels cannot reach international guests.
Repeating the same cleaning steps every week.

scenes.win: Yes. eBay solves it like this: Around 2 billion live listings from sellers worldwide, many of them one-of-a-kind.
scenes.lose: You fixed a problem these users rarely have. Hint: one thing that frustrates them is "fakes and condition disputes".

scenes.title: Build the core
scenes.prompt: You can build one thing first. Which feature becomes the heart of eBay?
right: Auctions and Buy It Now: sellers choose bidding or a fixed price, with Best Offer for haggling.

wrong.text: Practo Prime for doctors: paid plan with better visibility, booking tools and support.
Free cancellation and pay at property: many rooms can be cancelled free until a set date and paid on arrival.
Public gallery and Discord community: everyone can see others' images and prompts, and chat in Discord.
Pause membership: freeze your pass for some days when you travel or are sick.
Calm Health: a version for employers and health plans, with screening, personalised programmes and reporting.

scenes.win: Good call. Auctions find a fair price for rare items where nobody knows the true value.
scenes.lose: Users shrug. That feature belongs to a different kind of product. Hint: eBay's promise is "For buyers: the widest choice of used, rare and collectible items, with a refund promise."

scenes.title: Make money
scenes.prompt: Investors ask: where will most of eBay's money come from?
right: Final value fees: about 13.6% of the total sale price in most US categories, plus about $0.30 to $0.40 per order.

wrong.text: Energy supply: selling electricity and gas to homes and businesses; the vast majority of the roughly £13 billion revenue.
Business and Enterprise seats: $19 and $39 per user a month; the biggest revenue source.
Business delivery: fees from businesses including Reliance's JioMart.
Finance commission (old model): lenders paid Cazoo a cut for each finance deal arranged.
InstaHelp: hourly house help; ₹71 crore NTV in Q2 FY27, still loss-making.

scenes.win: That's it. eBay makes money in two main ways: a final value fee on each sale, and ads that sellers buy to rank higher.
scenes.lose: Revenue barely moves, and runway shrinks. Hint, look at how eBay prices things: "Free to list up to 250 items a month in the US."

elevenlabs.section: AI tools for creating and building
elevenlabs.summary: ElevenLabs makes computer voices that sound like real people.
lessons: Quality can be the whole strategy.
Serve both creators and enterprises.
Build a two-sided market where you can.

scenes.title: Who is it for?
scenes.prompt: Day 1. You are the new PM of ElevenLabs. AI voice company that turns text into lifelike speech in 70+ languages, clones voices, dubs videos and powers talking AI agents. Who do you build for first?

openevidence.section: AI tools for creating and building
openevidence.summary: OpenEvidence is like ChatGPT, but only for doctors and nurses.
lessons: Vertical AI wins on trust. Picking only vetted sources and showing citations beat general chatbots for doctors.
The user and the payer can be different.
A verified audience can be worth more than a big audience.

scenes.title: Who is it for?
scenes.prompt: Day 1. You are the new PM of OpenEvidence. A free AI search tool that answers doctors' medical questions using trusted journals, with sources cited. Who do you build for first?
